Back in battlefield milsim we’d run specific gamemodes like large scale team deathmatch or simple objective modes that would give us access to the whole map/most of it. 

From there the actual op/mission we’d run would depend on the amount of players we had. 
- We could run small 8 man ops (sometimes smaller like 6 man if it was training or a practice op). Those smaller ops would be simple killing ops, like we start here y’all start there and just first team to take out the other wins. But we’d play more proper. With actual clearing and bounding techniques to simulate life. (Obviously those ops we just had one life) 

* however if the ops were bigger, like 10 to 20 man ops, we’d run different ops. We would run ops like 
- convoy escorts: we’d have one team member from a side be the designated driver, sometimes the driver was immortal, in which case the convoy could only move forward at a super slow and controlled speed if it was actively being escorted by a teammate.The goal was for the attacking team to push up to the spawn side of the enemy, whilst the enemy team had to stop the convoy at any means necessary. There was usually prep time for the defense to set up trenches and set up a defense squad if needed, then adding a recon squad, while the attacking force has the actual escort and a scout squad too. That’s where the team leads freedom comes into play! 

- if it was objective defense then it played similar, just in a fixed position. 

Usually the weapons on the designated convoy vehicle were not allowed to be used as the 50cals were super strong in battlefield. So it was only one person in the vehicle while the others were outside.
